pageTitle: Supported Resource Types for AWS Config
whatThePageStates: The page is a single flat catalogue of the AWS resource types that AWS Config can record, grouped into 130 service sections (H2 headings) and, inside those, 170 service sub-group labels in the 'AWS Service' column. Every entry is a row in a five-column table: AWS Service, Resource Type Value, Relationship, Related Resource, Notes. There are 645 rows that carry a Resource Type Value; the Relationship and Related Resource columns add ~201 further continuation rows that describe relationships for a resource type already listed, and carry no new resource type. The page asserts support in one direction only: appearing in the list means AWS Config can record that type. It states no per-resource-type 'No', gives no Region breakdown, and explicitly delegates Region availability, Advanced Query support and Proactive Evaluation support to three other pages by link.

features.featureName: Supported Resource Types for AWS Config (configuration recording)
features.collapse: Elastic Load Balancing gets five Resource Type Value rows but names only four distinct type identifiers: the 'Application Load Balancer' row and the 'Network Load Balancer' row both resolve to AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer. Those two ELB rows are marketing-name rows over one CloudFormation type, so 645 rows collapse to 644 distinct AWS::Service::Type strings. No other identifier repeats anywhere on the page.
features.statuses: 645 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 645+0+0=645. Support is stated only by presence: the table has no status column, so every listed row is an implicit Yes and there is nothing on the page that reads as an explicit No. The Notes column is non-empty on just 15 rows and never carries a negative status - 11 rows note that deletion events may take 120 or 360 hours to appear, and 4 note that the type's metadata is folded into another CI (AWS::S3::Bucket, AWS::IAM::User, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::Group). Those 4 are still listed as supported types, not as exclusions. The only explicit not-supported language on the page is prose, not rows: the CloudFormation footnote says Config does not record changes for stack member types that are not yet supported, and the CodePipeline footnote names CodeCommit repository, CodeDeploy application, ECS cluster and ECS service as appearing only in supplementary configuration. Those four names are not table rows and must not be harvested as No values against the axis. The intro tagging note warns that some resource types do not carry tag data but never enumerates which, so it produces no per-row status either.
features.scope: None on this page. Region is named and then handed off: the intro and the Note block both send the reader to 'Resource Coverage by Region Availability' for which types exist in which Region, and add that a type supported in at least one Region can be enabled for recording in all Regions. Advanced Query support and Proactive Evaluation support are likewise stated to be subsets of this list and delegated to a GitHub schema directory and to evaluate-config_components.html. So the page carries exactly one unqualified dimension - the resource type - and every second dimension is a link to somewhere else.
features.reasoning: The row's unit of claim is the Resource Type Value cell: that is the identifier a customer puts into a recording configuration, and it is the only column that changes per row in a way that expresses coverage. Service is a grouping label spanning rows via rowspan, and Relationship / Related Resource describe a graph edge between two already-listed types rather than a new supported thing. resourceType from the external vocabulary is exact - the AWS::Service::Type namespace exists independently of AWS Config, which is merely declaring which members of it it can record.

shouldNotExtract: The 'See also' section at the foot is AI-coding-assistant boilerplate about the Agent Toolkit and aws agent-toolkit search-skills - it is not coverage and must be dropped, including its H2, which is present in the .md twin but not an H2 in the HTML. The Relationship and Related Resource columns are a resource graph, not a coverage axis: values like 'is attached to', 'is associated with', 'is contained in', 'EC2 instance', 'Subnet', 'Virtual private cloud (VPC)', 'S3 bucket', 'IAM role' are relationship prose and the ~201 continuation rows that hold them carry no Resource Type Value at all. The standalone twelve-row 'Attributes / Description' table in the Amazon Simple Storage Service section (AccelerateConfiguration, BucketAcl, BucketPolicy, CrossOriginConfiguration, LifecycleConfiguration, LoggingConfiguration, NotificationConfiguration, ReplicationConfiguration, RequestPaymentConfiguration, TaggingConfiguration, WebsiteConfiguration, VersioningConfiguration) is a list of S3 bucket sub-attributes Config tracks, has only two columns, and is not part of the resource-type axis. All 34 repeated 'AWS Service | Resource Type Value | Relationship | Related Resource | Notes' header rows and their separator rows are structure. The asterisk footnotes under EC2, ECS, S3, CloudFormation, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, Config and Systems Manager are explanatory prose; the trailing '*' glued to nine resource type values (AWS::EC2::Host*, AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup*, AWS::ECS::Service*, AWS::S3::Bucket*, AWS::S3::BucketPolicy*, AWS::CloudFormation::Stack*, AWS::CodeBuild::Project*, AWS::CodePipeline::Pipeline*, AWS::Config::ResourceCompliance*, AWS::Config::ConfigurationRecorder*) is a footnote marker and not a status - it must be stripped, not read as Partial. The 'Important' monthly-cadence banner, the Note block on Region availability and tagging, the four intro bullets of cross-references, and the periodic-rules explanation with its 'The provided resource ID and resource type cannot be found' error string are all narrative.
coverageDimensions: RESOURCE TYPE: this is the only dimension the page actually measures. It gives 645 rows and 644 distinct AWS::Service::Type identifiers, all supported, no negatives. SERVICE: given only as an ambiguous grouping, never as a claim. There are two incompatible service counts on one page - 130 H2 section headings (129 distinct, because 'Amazon Lex' appears twice) and 170 distinct labels in the 'AWS Service' column, since a single H2 like 'Amazon CloudWatch' spans six sub-groups (CloudWatch, Application Signals, Internet Monitor, Logs, RUM, Evidently). One heading is also simply wrong: the second 'Amazon Lex' H2 carries the anchor amazonqbusiness and heads the Amazon Q Business rows. The page never says any service is unsupported, so no service-level No exists and any 'AWS Config covers N services' figure is a derived guess, not a stated number. REGION: nothing. The page states zero Region facts and twice sends the reader elsewhere for them; any per-Region number attributed to this page is fabricated. It does state one Region-adjacent rule in prose - a type supported in at least one Region can be enabled for recording in all Config Regions - but that is a policy sentence, not an enumeration, and yields no count. Likewise nothing quantitative for Advanced Queries or Proactive Evaluation: both are called subsets of this list, and both subsets live on other pages.
trap: The dominant trap is counting table rows instead of Resource Type Value cells. The HTML holds ~893 <tr> elements, but only 645 carry a resource type; the rest are rowspan continuation rows that repeat a type to add another Relationship / Related Resource pair (Elastic Load Balancing, CodePipeline, EC2 and CloudTrail all do this), plus 34 repeated header rows and the 13-row S3 attributes table. A parser that counts <tr> reports ~893 supported resource types, a ~38 percent overstatement. Runners-up, in order. (1) Regex-sweeping the page for /AWS::[A-Za-z0-9]+::[A-Za-z0-9]+/ yields 660 occurrences, because Notes cells, footnotes and the intro re-mention already-listed types; deduplicating that sweep gives 644, which accidentally matches the distinct-target count and so looks correct while being arrived at wrongly - it silently drops the second ELB row. (2) Treating the trailing footnote asterisk on nine values as a Partial or caveated status, inventing a tri-state the page does not have. (3) Reading the CodePipeline footnote's 'CodeCommit repository, CodeDeploy application, ECS cluster, and ECS service' as four explicit No rows, when they are prose about stack members and ECS service is in fact a supported type (AWS::ECS::Service) elsewhere on the same page. (4) Counting H2 headings as services and reporting 130 or 131 - 131 wrongly includes the injected 'See also' boilerplate section, 130 double-counts 'Amazon Lex', and neither number is a coverage claim. (5) Trusting the .md twin's structure: it renders 96 sections as bullet lists and only 34 as pipe tables, and its converter mislabels the AWS::EC2::VPCGatewayAttachment row, promoting the type into a bold group header and leaving 'Resource Type Value: NA' behind - a table-only parser would miss that row and a value-only parser would emit a literal 'NA' resource type. (6) Attaching a Region count to this page when it states none.
